# Finding ∫ -3x⁴sin(x) dx

I'll use the **tabular integration by parts** method, differentiating the polynomial and integrating the trig function repeatedly.

## Setting Up the Table

| Sign | Differentiate (D) | Integrate (I) |
|------|-------------------|---------------|
| +    | -3x⁴             | sin(x)        |
| -    | -12x³            | -cos(x)       |
| +    | -36x²            | -sin(x)       |
| -    | -72x             | cos(x)        |
| +    | -72              | sin(x)        |
| -    | 0                | -cos(x)       |

## Multiplying Along the Diagonals

$$\begin{aligned}
&(+1)(-3x^4)(-\cos x) = 3x^4\cos x \\
&(-1)(-12x^3)(-\sin x) = -12x^3\sin x \\
&(+1)(-36x^2)(\cos x) = -36x^2\cos x \\
&(-1)(-72x)(\sin x) = 72x\sin x \\
&(+1)(-72)(-\cos x) = 72\cos x
\end{aligned}$$

## Verification

Differentiating the result:
- d/dx[3x⁴cos(x)] = 12x³cos(x) - 3x⁴sin(x)
- d/dx[-12x³sin(x)] = -36x²sin(x) - 12x³cos(x)
- d/dx[-36x²cos(x)] = -72xcos(x) + 36x²sin(x)
- d/dx[72xsin(x)] = 72sin(x) + 72xcos(x)
- d/dx[72cos(x)] = -72sin(x)

All terms cancel except **-3x⁴sin(x)** ✓

## Final Answer

<answer>3*x**4*cos(x) - 12*x**3*sin(x) - 36*x**2*cos(x) + 72*x*sin(x) + 72*cos(x) + C</answer>
